subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be based on live gateway runtime health, a passive local plugin status contract, or the current `not checked`/`status --all` split?
rationale: Current main mitigates the old wording but does not implement the live-runtime health contract requested here, and the remaining fix shape overlaps the broader open issue and a conflicting fork PR.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599` the canonical path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase and prove `status --deep` plus JSON output against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept current behavior
options.body: Declare `not checked` plus opt-in `status --all` memory inspection sufficient, then close the fork PR and this issue with release evidence.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599` the canonical path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work places the central shared status memory surface under this contributor’s recent history, and the remaining decision is about the status/doctor boundary rather than one plugin.
